1202014 Hopefully a (perhaps temporary) fix for the synthetic stack bug.
2f1243e Add a `with(MetadataKey<Boolean>)` method to set a boolean metadata flag.

229fbca Convert Metadata.EMPTY to a static method
d2250ab Add pom file generation to Flogger

=== 2f1243e ===
commit 2f1243e5df8a6601568c41e4136ab7f7c2504fa8
Author: dbeaumont <dbeaumont@google.com>
Date:   Thu May 7 23:25:00 2020 -0700

    Add a `with(MetadataKey<Boolean>)` method to set a boolean metadata flag.
    
    I've been meaning to look at this for a while and there are hundreds of uses of just this key which would be improved visually:
    
      `logger.atWarning().with(PERSISTENT, true).log("...");`
    would become:
      `logger.atWarning().with(PERSISTENT).log("...");`
    
    RELNOTES=Added `with(MetadataKey<Boolean>)` method for setting metadata "flags".

commit 0805f96dfea828ef444c4415f7180474225e3d9f
Author: cgb <cgb@google.com>
Date:   Thu Jan 23 14:29:51 2020 -0800

    Explicitly allow logVarargs to take an array containing null objects.
    
    This is already supported for log() calls which take @NullableDect Object
    params and then pass them into logImpl (see
    http://third_party/java_src/flogger/api/src/main/java/com/google/common/flogger/LogContext.java?rcl=289240473&l=896).
    
    This is so a @FormatMethod which uses "@Nullable Object... args" can pass the
    args directly to logVarargs() without a static analysis test failing.
    
    RELNOTES=Explicitly allow an array containing null objects in logVarargs().
    
    -------------
    Created by MOE: https://github.com/google/moe
    MOE_MIGRATED_REVID=291245533

Author: dbeaumont <dbeaumont@google.com>
Date:   Sat Jan 11 04:43:10 2020 -0800

    Adding "callerOf(Class<?>)" to LogSites to allow simpler APIs for logging utilities.
    
    This avoids people needing to expose "LogSite" as a parameter in logging helper classes and should allow most of the current ~350 call sites using it to be simplified.
    
    This is a retry of the previous change which accidentally broke anyone who was relying on being able to set an INVALID log site to suppress log site determination (that's apparently a thing in Android).
    
    RELNOTES=Adding "callerOf(Class<?>)" to LogSites.

Author: dbeaumont <dbeaumont@google.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 25 05:10:47 2019 -0700

    Promoting with() method to public FluentLogger since it's starting to be useful outside of GoogleLogger (there's a thread in open source where I just recommended it to someone forgetting that it's not public).
    
    This went through API review before, and there have been no issues with it internally, but it's not used super heavily (which is good, since it's "advanced mode") so it's not been through a proper "trial by fire" inside [] really.
    
    If anyone can think of any reason for _not_ doing this, please speak up!
    
    Relnotes:
      - Promoting the "`with()`" method from `GoogleLogger` to `FluentLogger`.
        - This is useful to piggyback semantic information _about_ the log statement into For example, identifying special log statements which should be handled differently (e.g. sent to a different log file).

Author: dbeaumont <dbeaumont@google.com>
Date:   Tue Jul 24 12:03:29 2018 -0700

    Adding a way to explicitly get the logSite information and loosening up the withInjectedLogSite() call to permit users to call it (with docs explaining why). This is a neat way to solve a lot of the cases where people were splitting the logging API out.
    
    LogSite needed to be split out from the main "api" target so it can be exported separately along with the LogSites class; which needs to be separate since it depends on the Platform class. It's a bit of a mess, but it mostly works (it also means there's a separate target for anyone messing about with log sites, so it's easy to track).
    
    RELNOTES=Support explicit log site injection for logging helper methods.
    
    -------------
    Created by MOE: https://github.com/google/moe
    MOE_MIGRATED_REVID=206129913

**(2) Specific change that introduced the bug:** Commit `02a5f3f` removed the `skip` parameter from `CallerFinder.getStackForCallerOf(...)` and changed the search loop from `for (int index = skip; ...)` to `for (int index = 0; ...)`. It also updated the call site in `LogContext.java` from `getStackForCallerOf(LogContext.class, new Throwable(), 2, stackSize.getMaxDepth())` to `getStackForCallerOf(LogContext.class, new Throwable(), stackSize.getMaxDepth())`, dropping the explicit skip-count of 2. The commit's own rationale (stated in its added comment, later reused almost verbatim in the fix commit's diff for removal) was that skip counts were "problematic in the face of things like Proguard." However, this removed the ability to skip over intermediate `LogContext`-subclass `postProcess()` frames on the stack, causing `getStackForCallerOf` to stop its scan at the wrong frame (an internal framework frame belonging to a subclass override) instead of the true user call site, whenever `postProcess()` was overridden.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** The bug-fixing commit's diff directly re-adds a `skip` parameter to the exact same method signature and loop that `02a5f3f` had modified, with an explanatory comment describing precisely the override scenario (`OtherChildContext::postProcess` / `ChildContext::postProcess` frames sitting between the true caller and `LogContext::postProcess`) that `index = 0` (no skipping) fails to handle correctly.
